podcast.title: Dislike for Doo-wop and "You Cheated"
podcast.body: Despite his involvement with the hit doo-wop track "You Cheated," Frankie Ervin generally disliked the doo-wop genre and found "You Cheated" to be a particularly bad example of it. He only agreed to record it for career reasons, as he was actively seeking a solo career at the time. "Irving hated the song. He didn't like Doop generally, and he thought the song was a particularly bad example of the genre."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Frustration Over Lack of Credit for The Shields
podcast.body: Frankie Ervin was annoyed when "You Cheated" was released under the group name The Shields rather than as a solo record by him, despite him performing the lead vocals. The label's decision was reportedly a strategic move to avoid promoting a solo singer who might later demand money and royalties. "Frankie Irving was naturally annoyed, that he wasn't given the label credit for the record."

podcast.title: Reputation for Novelty Cash-in Records
podcast.body: While a member of Charles Brown's group, Frankie Ervin developed a reputation for performing novelty "cash-in" records. This included tracks like "Dragnet Blues," which led to a lawsuit, and his version of "Johnny Ace's Last Letter," demonstrating his knack for capitalizing on popular trends and events. "While with Brown's group, he developed a reputation for being able to perform novelty cash in records."
